title: Disappointing treatment of loyal premium subscribers
body: I’m a premium yearly subscriber and have been enjoying the app an its features. However, a recent update has left me feeling undervalued as a loyal customer. The app introduced family sharing which sounds great, but if you previously subscribed on their premium yearly plan, they will charge you $59.99 a year to add this. Existing premium subscribers like myself are essentially being told that our loyalty doesn’t matter and need to pay double to get family sharing. When I talked with support, they said that it was to cover “data costs.” This reasoning doesn’t hold up. Family sharing doesn’t generate additional data costs per user in any meaningful way that justifies excluding existing premium subscribers. What’s truly disappointing is the principle: when you introduce something new, loyal subscribers should already paid for premium shouldn’t be treated as second-class customers. This feels like a bait and switch tactic by punishing early adopters instead of rewarding them. If you’re considering this app,be aware that “premium” doesn’t mean you’ll receive future premium features. You’ll most likely be told to pay again. I expected better from a weather app I trusted and supported

title: Deleted within 2 minutes
body: Within the first 10 seconds of using the app it asks if I’m enjoying the app and for feedback. Clicked on 2 different things trying to learn/navigate the app and it asks again if I’m enjoying the app. No. No I am not. I’ll stick to Radarscope.

body: Saved locations work sometimes, and other times all the toggles don’t work for saved locations. For $39.99 you could do some QA work and get that right. Really not useful to me if I can’t turn on the features I like. I renewed hoping that had been fixed, but it hasn’t.

title: Junk…

title: Free version is unusable
body: I had to delete this app. The whole thing is a nag screen. Don’t make it available for free if you’re going remind me on every transition and button tap that you want me to subscribe. Even trying to add the app widget brings you to the paywall. For context, I’m not looking for everything to be free. I bought Dark Sky because I thought the experience was great. Developers need money, I get it. Here, the experience really isn’t great. The predictions are very similar to Apple Weather (Dark Sky IP) and it’s been difficult to access the kinds of details that would really differentiate the two. There’s also some consistent, annoying latency when scrolling over buttons that randomly registers a button tap—and often brings me to a nag screen bc it’s a (basic and unmarked) “premium” feature. This app feels like a disingenuous money grab hoping that an alt color palette and an air of premium quality will generate lots of subscription revenue. But there’s a kind of sad desperation in how much the UI asks for money.

title: I tried feedback but it didn’t work
body: This is a BEAUTIFUL app. I mean, you can tell they spent loads of time making this thing pretty. But oh my goodness, it is buggy. It might be the most buggy paid app I’ve used. From freezing when it opens, glitchy touch points, unresponsive menus, to overheating my battery and completing freezing to where it never recovers. I want this to be Darksky so badly that I wanted to give feedback (which I never do), but the feedback form was bugged. After 3 attempts, I finally got it pop-up a message saying I don’t have email set up on my phone. So, here I am putting in a review hoping that the developer reads this. Heck, if you want to open source it or bring on contributors, let me know.. because I want to see something beautiful deliver great weather content.

title: Not Dark Sky lol
body: To compare your self to the greatest weather app of all time is egregious when your features are your shortcomings. The app takes entirely too long to load on start. Slow to open then incredibly slow to fetch data. Weather is a quick look and the sluggishness of the fancy UI is an utter failure. The UI also takes entirely too many clicks to get anywhere of interest. Swiping, dragging and clicking is too much when the native iOS weather app just shows you literally everything this app does upfront on open without delay. Over the trial there were 4 weather events in my area and I received 0 notifications. Hard pass.

I haven’t even experienced the app yet, but I’m already being pressured to sign up for a paid plan. This constant push toward memberships and subscriptions in every app is getting exhausting.

body: I love the look and the potential. Living in Florida I love the tropics feature to see the current activity for hurricanes and depressions. I have two screenshots one from the Apple Weather App and one from Element. It was raining and that was shown in Apple Weather App. Element showed nothing on radar. I hope it gets better but if not I wish I could have gotten money back but I guess they have till my year is up to improve before I cancel.

body: Decent all at first. Didn’t quite feel like dark sky, but as close as I’ve seen. Recently seems something broke within it. Getting spammed with false advisory warnings (air quality, fog, frost, etc). Multiple coming through for different locations almost back to back giving pages of notifications — even clicking them direct brings you to the app with no sign of where that alert even came from. App seems to be running a bit clunky as well. No real benefit over the stock app outside of daily (morning and evening updates).

I get that for being out and about and needing weather, but while i am at my desk preparing to go out, i am using my phone for calls and such and need a desktop weather report which would be the iPad. Future forecasts hard to read - make it easy for us to see what it’s going to be like tomorrow, the weekend. Basically: Good info, not great display.

Only the wind speed and gusts. Maybe I’m missing something? So far the AccuWeather app has been the nicest format for me even though it doesn’t seem to be all that accurate at times.

title: Poor performance
body: Don’t bother trying to use half the functionality the app promises. The radar doesn’t load, doesn’t play, and the summaries are clearly AI generated slop. Better off checking your local paper. At least a person wrote that.

title: Potential
body: I got the app and have been using the free trial for three or four days now. The app is very clean looking and there is plenty of data. However, there are some basic issues that led me to not continue past the free trial. Primarily, the time sliders on the radar screen are nearly impossible to move. Most of the time, I can’t move them at all. I also can’t switch from the precipitation map. Basic issues like this are why the subscription price is not worth it to me.

title: No CarPlay support
body: I got excited when I saw that it had most of the features of Weather On The Way and Carrot but there isn’t integration of CarPlay. What good is the navigation weather feature if you can’t pull it up while traveling?

title: Pretty but not very accurate data
body: Seems to not have great data sources. For instance right now we are in an air quality event with warnings about severe air quality and this app says air quality is good.

title: Could be a LOT better
body: Hi Element devs! I have to say, as someone who used to use Dark Sky before Apple ruined it, this app has some SERIOUS potential!!! You guys are on the right track with this, but there’s some SEVERE bugs that prevent me from rating this higher than 2 stars. Firstly, the widgets don’t update in real time; you have to manually open the app for them to update as you change physical locations (for example, going to work or coming home). And secondly, the app seems to have trouble remembering that I have purchased the subscription, and it sometimes disables the widgets as a result, forcing me to open the app once again. When I do, it immediately throws the paywall in my face again, forcing me to tap the Restore Purchase button to make it go away and re-enable everything. It’s getting on my nerves now, so PLEASE fix this bug ASAP if you can! Thank you in advance!

title: Thought it would be better
body: I don’t download tons of weather apps, in fact I have installed a total of zero. However, I kept seeing ads for this and thought it looked nice and the design was amazing. So I downloaded it and immediately regretted it. First of all, almost every time I opened the app I get asked to buy premium (which seems way too expensive but I’m probably just poor) which makes this already off to a bad start. Secondly, the only thing I ever use the Apple Weather app for is for the widgets. Using widgets is a no-brainer for me, and yet it tells me it is locked behind Premium. And I don’t know if it is my phone (iPhone 13 Mini) or the app, but it runs horribly. I can’t even scroll through the settings without it running way below 60fps (maybe around 30). I don’t see how I am expected to use all of the nice overlays and map visualizers if I can’t even use the menu smoothly?

It's really annoying and there's not really a fix unfortunately Otherwise, I really like the app pay for it, but not at its current pricing

title: Promising but often unusably slow
body: I WANT to love this app. Great interface and nicely customizable. But especially after the last update, it’s soooooo slow loading weather info after opening that it’s basically unusable. Sticking with it in the hopes it’s improved, but at the moment can’t realistically recommend.

title: Inferior information density
body: I expected more customization for visualizations for the daily or weekly views. In the daily view, you get a single graph line (temperature, precipitation chance, etc) along with cloud cover icons per hour. The view shows 6h on screen (at least on my iPhone 16). Compare to Carrot, where you see about a 15h window, and you get cloud cover, likely precipitation by hour, and one metric of your choice. In Carrot, can also toggle to report in 2h blocks, doubling your window on screen to 1.5d. This really helps you digest the mid term weather without having to check back. Also compare to Wunderground daily view, where you get about 4d’s worth of graph on screen, with temp and precipitation both shown as continuous metrics, and by-day summaries for high/low temp, cloud cover, precip chance and amount. I far prefer the denser information views. I would not consider switching to Element without some improvements to how 12-24h range forecast data is displayed. The current UX could work for someone who isn’t coming in with specific habits. But the ad I saw mentioned Dark Sky, may it rest in peace, so I had very high expectations.

title: Great Ideas but Poor Implementation
body: The app follows a similar UI style as Apples weather app with the ability to customize layout and data as you choose. However there appears to be something wrong with the apps ability to utilize the 120hz smooth refresh rate (Apples Promotion). This results in a very stuttering scrolling experience that on the surface may not be a deal breaker until the experience coming from other apps and the general iOS interface. The developer needs to address this and the app would be a winner for one of the best weather applications in the store.

title: Sleek but glitchy
body: this app has a sleek interface but doesn’t work in the way I want. My favorite feature of weather apps is the radar and this one has an unreliable radar that won’t play future activity. Therefore deleting the app.

title: Smooth interface, lacking features, hope there’s more to come
body: App is an overall smooth interface which is nice. Customizations are pretty good too. I’m not exactly used to the weather radar color scheme compared to every other radar/weather app I use so that will take some getting use to. For paying a subscription I’d expect more from the app. For some reason I was expecting a customized forecast for activities not just driving. Tell me good days and bad days for activities/events depending on conditions that I set (like weather underground used to have). I’d keep my subscription if it had that. Testing it out this week to see how fast and accurate it is.

title: Good app, but not my #1 pick.
body: Honestly, I rather enjoy this app. I like the aesthetic, a lot. It has nice functionality as well. However, comparing it to my current daily use app (Carrot), it does fall very far from surpassing the quality of Carrot. Element lacks features that I personally find important (like stargazing info, lightning strike reports, etc) and for some reason is quite laggy on my phone (iPhone 16PM). The lag is the biggest deal-breaker, personally. Hopefully the app continues to receive updates and build further, because it’s quite promising.

title: Clean but the radar is lacking
body: I want to like this and support it but I’d like to see radar for storms. This seems to be a basic feature that every other weather app has. I do care about precipitation but I want to see the radar for storms and severe weather and don’t see that anywhere.

title: Enough subscriptions
body: Love how the app functions but enough of the subscriptions already.

title: Too soon to tell
body: This app is very young, but the interface seems right for being a Dark Sky alternate. I’m using this app on a iPhone 16 Pro and it seems to be developed for a 60hz display which is fine but a little painful to use on a 120hz. I will upgrade this to 4 stars if the weather is accurate, but for now great job developers on creating an aesthetically pleasing app!

title: It’s beautiful but…
body: There was a storm right above me and this app didn’t show real time. Sadly, the apple weather app was more accurate which blew my mind.

title: No widget? No complication? No dice.
body: App itself is fine, but I interact with my weather app almost exclusively via Lock Screen widgets and watch complication. I’m not paying $49.99 a year in 2025 for an app that doesn’t provide either of those, and only a very limited Home Screen widget (no hourly option). Will happily revisit if and when dev adds these, or prices it more reasonably for lacking those features most competitors offer at roughly the same subscription price.

title: Great for the General Public
body: This app works as a basic weather app that’s clean. However, the maps leave a lot to be desired. It’s definitely not for the hardcore weather fans or for those that need to see the radar.

title: It’s okay
body: I used the free trial and I guess it was okay. I wanted to really like it, but I sent these people several emails and I was not able to get any of them answered. The morning and evening update never seemed to get delivered at the times that they were supposed to. I either ended up getting them much later or not at all. Also, I’m in Omaha/Millard, but this app sent me messages and updates from Chalco? That’s in Sarpy County. Maybe one day I’ll be back. However this app seems to have a long way to go.

title: Question
body: Why do I see promos to upgrade to premium? I am already paying for that, right?

title: Display Stuttering and Too Many Taps
body: Beautiful app with plenty of data but I do feel like a lot of that data is hidden away behind cards and swipes. A little too minimal for my tastes but the overall design is gorgeous. On an iPhone 15 Pro Max with iOS 18.5 I’m seeing some stuttering while scrolling as if I had battery saver turned on. Definitely not a smooth experience in that regard.

title: Beautiful
body: Beautiful app. Probably my favorite weather UI. But, it needs to be quicker. Feels like city switching is slow. Loading is slower than I’m used to. Need widgets. Has the potential to be at Flighty level of UI/UX.

body: I’m looking forward to this being available on MacOS, and am excited about its performance on iOS. However, the MacOS version so far fails to connect to element servers upon launch, requiring a force quit to get out of a “retry?” loop. I’m writing this review to get the developer’s attention! Go Element!!!

title: Nice looking but needs features
body: I downloaded this from an ad that said it was like DarkSky, which was my favorite app. I really like the aesthetics here it has great potential. But I couldn’t get UV Index to show, no matter what I did. I liked that I could place that stat above temperature (or anywhere I wanted ) but I still could not get UV index to display for my location in the US. I will check back in a few months or so to see if there are changes.

title: Great start with some missing features
body: As someone always looking for new weather apps (someone help me please), I think they’ve nailed the basics so far. I’m sure these are in the pipeline, but seems like there’s no Home Screen or Lock Screen widgets. Haven’t had any significant weather to test notifications yet, so not sure if there is support for Live Activities. Hoping for regular updates but not sure I can replace Carrot just yet until there’s better feature parity.

title: A great weather app with tough to swallow pricing
body: I really like this weather app. It has a creative radar forward way of viewing weather, which is my preferred option. However, the cost to upgrade to premium is a little ridiculous for a weather app at $50/year.

title: Faulty Notifications
body: I keep getting notifications for fog and frost when it’s over 50 degrees F here. No fog and certainly no frost at that temperature. I double checked my location and it’s correct. UPDATE: First of all, thanks to the developer for responding quickly to my issue! I tried turning off notifications and since I turned them back on the problem seems to have corrected itself. I’m now very happy with the app!

title: Best new weather app
body: Refreshing new take on the forecast that feels designed for this era. Radar is great and I love the Lock Screen widgets and use them every day!

title: Best weather app
body: Best weather app ever it’s so simple and easy, barely no ads and it’s so cool and go show some love to the Instagram

title: everything at a glance
body: well.lsid pit app.all the weather and radar is thoughtfully displayed. notifications are right on time.

title: Design Masterclass
body: So worth it! An awesome, beautifully designed app. It’s straightforward and provides precise real-time information through a clean, simple UI. There’s nothing else out there this elegant or thoughtfully built. Absolutely love the routes feature. It makes planning my day effortless. 10/10

title: Great new app!
body: Downloaded the app not knowing what to expect, but the design is very sleek and gives me everything I need to use day to day.

title: New Go-to
body: This has become my new go-to weather app, replacing the iOS app most of the time.

title: Already subscribed
body: I like the app, but it keeps asking me to subscribe and I'm already subscribed. It's very annoying to have to tell it that I'm already subscribed each time I open the app. I sent an email to your support email address but I never got a reply or a resolution to the issue. The one star (see Update below) is due to the problem, not the app itself. I'll update the review if and when it ever gets fixed. If I don't hear back soon, I'm gonna request a refund. Update: The developer got back to me and the issue has been resolved. I've updated the review from 1 to 5 stars. The main feature I like about this app is that I can view weather patterns for up to 12 hours in the future. I realize that weather is a very chaotic system, but this gives me a general idea of what to expect. Have that right?

title: Awesome New Weather App!!
body: really good weather app. radar is fast and looks cool, use it every day now. I like how adding a new location is super easy too!

title: So far . . . AWESOME!
body: My initial reaction is that it’s well thought out and beautifully simple in its design. Amazing. Now we learn about its accuracy. Also, I love the idea of forecast along a route. It doesn’t seem to customize departure time though. And I’m waiting to see if truly gives forecast changes along the way and any local alerts. If so, it’s a total package and game-changer for me!

title: Add more country’s!
body: I live in Dominican Republic, the app don’t work here. But the app is beautiful great work!

title: Great new app
body: I like how clean it looks and how easy it is to save locations!

title: Must have app
body: This app has a great vibe to it, I would say more comforting and cozy that other weather apps don’t have. Also love the fact that it gives details about the specific place I’m in. Great app that is worth the money.

title: Wonderful
body: Element is a beautifully crafted weather app where the developers care and attention to detail really shine through. It’s rare to find such a refined and capable app.

title: Awesome Weather App
body: Works perfectly!
